text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- A planned international donors' conference for reconstruction aid, scheduled for June 24 and 25, is looking more and more uncertain with some countries proposing the postponement of the conference until July 15, says foreign trade minister, Hasan Muratovic.

- Bosnia's Serb republic agreed to borrow 3.8 million from Moslem-Croat federation to allow it to pay off its debt to the World Bank. By accepting this money from the federation, the Serb entity has at last recognised the fact that only the country of Bosnia has international status, Muratovic says.
- Foreign affairs minister, Jadranko Prlic, denies media reports that he and co-prime minister in the Bosnian government, Haris Silajdzic, will soon visit the Yugoslav capital Belgrade.

- The current peace in Bosnia is only a prelude to a new war, says General Martin Spegelj, retired Croatian defence minister, in an interview in which he criticises some aspects of the Dayton peace agreement.

- "Bosnia's Sava river valley was handed over to the Serbs despite all claims to the contrary by Croatian political leaders. There was not a single reason for our huge forces to withdraw from there," Spegelj says.

- Bosnian Serbs plan to build an airport on Mount Romanija, 40 km (25 miles) east of Sarajevo, and it is obvious that this is an idea from Belgrade which serves military not economic purposes, commentary says.
- The Bosnian PTT says it will send out new, smaller telephone bills after the federation prime minister, Edhem Bicakcic, accused it of illegal price hikes of up to 400 percent.

- Outgoing international High Representative, Carl Bildt, says in farewell address on Bosnian television that the international community will never tolerate a new war in Bosnia, ethnic partition or domination of one nation over another. --Sarajevo newsroom +387-71-663-864
